summary: The scale evolution of parton distributions is governed by splitting functions. We compute the four-loop splitting functions in perturbative QCD that control the evolution of quark nonsinglet distributions. title: Emergent Kinetic Constraints and Subspace Fragmentation in Rydberg Arrays
summary: In a strongly interacting Rydberg atom array, the dynamics are often constrained to the decoupled and fragmented Hilbert subspaces, representing an intriguing paradigm for nonergodicity. title: Plasma Conductivity from Warm Dense Matter to the Spitzer Limit Using Mean-Force Kinetic Theory
summary: A theoretical model is developed to compute electronic transport coefficients extending from warm and dense to hot and dilute plasma conditions. This kinetic theory-based approach models strong Coulomb correlations by treating collisions using the potential of mean force, electron degeneracy using t…

summary: We simulate nanoscale ice-glass friction from first principles and upscale it by modeling frictional heating. summary: In topological materials, Berry curvature leads to intrinsic Hall responses. title: Nonperturbative Nonlinear Hall Effect in Nonequilibrium Steady States
summary: The nonlinear Hall effect in quantum materials has attracted broad interest, yet most existing studies focus on the weak-field, perturbative regime. title: Spontaneous Mean Flow Emerging from Electrohydrodynamic Turbulence in Nematic Liquid Crystals
summary: High-speed imaging and particle tracking, supported by nematohydrodynamic simulations, reveal a system-spanning mean flow that emerges spontaneously from fully developed turbulence in nematic liquid crystals.

title: Noise-Driven Odd Elastic Waves in Living Chiral Active Matter
summary: Chiral active matter is predicted to exhibit odd elasticity, with nontraditional elastic response arising from a combination of chirality, being out of equilibrium, and the presence of nonreciprocal interactions. title: Erratum: Bounds on Screened Dark Energy from Near-Earth Space-Based Measurements [Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 101002 (2026)]
Peierls Transition and Magnetism in a Dirac Semimetal: ${\mathrm{CaMnBi}}_{2}$
summary: Neutron and x-ray diffraction reveal a two-dimensional Peierls transition of Dirac electrons in CaMnBi , producing a zigzag bond-order distortion and corresponding Dirac band reconstruction in the bismuth layers rather than the previously proposed canted magnetism and associated Weyl state.

title: Fluctuation-Response Theory of Nonequilibrium Complex Fluids
summary: A framework for nonequilibrium steady states is developed that can be applied to complex fluids, including dense biological and active soft materials.

title: Incoherent Imaging with Spatially Structured Quantum Probes
summary: Researchers introduce spatially structured quantum-optical imaging techniques to overcome resolution limits and achieve quantum-enhanced absorption and fluorescence imaging.

title: Stability, Degeneracy, and Scalability of a 600-Site Cavity Array Microscope
summary: A scalable cavity array microscope architecture is presented, featuring over 600 independent optical cavities for parallelized light-matter interactions, providing opportunities for quantum networking and sensing applications.

title: Theory of Out-of-Time-Ordered Transport
summary: Researchers establish an effective field theory capturing late-time out-of-time-order correlators to uncover hidden transport parameters.

title: Spin Nematic Liquid Crystal and Scalar Spin Chirality in Tetragonal Lattice ${\mathrm{YbMnBi}}_{2}$
summary: Neutron scattering experiments on reveal that a dynamic spin nematic state coupled to magnetic fields generates scalar spin chirality, driving anomalous Hall and Nernst effects in the paramagnetic phase.

title: Phonon-Activated Collective Hopping in a Superionic Phase
summary: Observations of collective hopping in superionic agryodites improves the microscopic understanding of transport in these materials.

title: Generation of Large Coherent-State Superpositions in Free-Space Optical Pulses
summary: Researchers generate large-amplitude optical cat states in free space, establishing a vital building block for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Bounded-Error Quantum Simulation via Hamiltonian and Lindbladian Learning
summary: Researchers introduce a framework that infers quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.
